I'll read the batch-9 draft, the CIS results, and the reviewer notes, then fix the revert path and the KVM recovery paste.The revert path can die after the tar extract. I'll check `pam-auth-update` on Johnny, then fix that path and the KVM fallback.`man pam-auth-update` on Johnny allows several profile names on `--enable` and `--disable`, plus `--force`. I'll put faillock reset before that call and add a root-shell recovery that only extracts the tar.The revert helper no longer dies after the tar extract, and KVM recovery has a sudo-free path that only restores the tar.

## Detail

`docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh` and `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.md` are revised. Nothing was run on Johnny except a read of `man pam-auth-update`. `bash -n` on the script is clean. The CSV and the handoff were not touched.

**Revert helper.** `write_revert` now does this, in order:

1. Extract `/root/batch9-pam-security.tar`.
2. `faillock --user aj --reset || true` immediately, so a later non-zero exit cannot leave `aj` locked.
3. `pam-auth-update --force --disable … --enable unix`, with `|| echo WARN-pam-auth-update`. The tar-restored `common-*` files do not match the md5sums `pam-auth-update` recorded, and the man page says it will refuse a locally modified stack unless `--force` is given. A failure here is non-fatal. The extracted files are already the stock stack.
4. Remove the five profiles and the shell and pwquality drop-ins, then restore `chage` from `/root/batch9-chage.before`.
5. After those steps, require that `/etc/pam.d/common-auth` has no `pam_faillock` and that `pam_unix` still has `nullok`. If that check fails it prints `STOP-common-auth-restore` and exits 1. The timer, Rollback, and PASTE 3 all call this same helper.

**KVM fallback.** PASTE 3 in the script is still the first choice: `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-9.sh 3`. The `## Rollback` section now also has a root-shell block, marked `# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (KVM)`, for when sudo, the script, or `pam-auth-update` cannot be used (root console login or `su -`):

```bash
tar -C / -xzf /root/batch9-pam-security.tar
faillock --user aj --reset
systemctl stop johnny-cis-batch9-revert.timer
```

The tar extract alone puts the pre-change `common-*` files back (`pam_unix.so nullok`, no `pam_faillock`).

**Other review notes.**

- `sudo -n -v` inside PASTE 1 and PASTE 2 runs as root. The script now prints `ROOT-SUDO-N-OK` and says so in a comment. The `aj` sudo test is starting PASTE 2 with `sudo bash` from a new SSH session.
- Johnny’s `pam-auth-update(8)` synopsis is `--disable profile [profile...]` and `--enable profile [profile...]` on one command, and `--force` is the administrator override for a locally modified stack. If the enable line in PASTE 1 still fails, PASTE 1 runs the revert.
- `active_bare` now calls the revert on `STOP-value` when `CHANGED=1`, same as `active_eq`. PASTE 2 stops the timer and exits `STOP-timer-still-active` if `timer_active` is still true.
- After the batch is kept, `TMOUT=900` is readonly and exported, so a new login shell drops an idle SSH session at 15 minutes. Sessions already open keep their old environment until the next login shell. Aging is only `chage` for `aj` plus `useradd -D` and `PASS_MAX_DAYS`. Root and any later password accounts are not passed to `chage`, and a re-audit of 5.4.1.1 or 5.4.1.5 can still flag them.

## Relay

Batch 9 rev: revert extracts the tar, resets faillock for aj (`|| true`), then `pam-auth-update --force` (`|| echo WARN-pam-auth-update`), then rm, chage, then a common-auth check (no pam_faillock, pam_unix still has nullok). PASTE 3 script form stays first. Rollback adds a root-shell fallback: `tar -C / -xzf /root/batch9-pam-security.tar`, `faillock --user aj --reset`, `systemctl stop johnny-cis-batch9-revert.timer`. Tar alone is the stock PAM stack. `sudo -n -v` is documented as root-only; aj’s proof is `sudo bash` on PASTE 2. `man pam-auth-update` on Johnny allows multiple names per `--enable`/`--disable` and `--force`. `active_bare` calls revert when CHANGED=1. PASTE 2 checks the timer is inactive. TMOUT=900 readonly drops new idle SSH at 15 min. Aging covers aj and useradd -D only.

## Outline

- Revert order
  - Tar extract
  - `faillock --user aj --reset || true`
  - `pam-auth-update --force` or `WARN-pam-auth-update`
  - Remove profiles and drop-ins, restore chage
  - `common-auth` must have no `pam_faillock` and must still have `nullok`
- KVM
  - PASTE 3 script form first
  - Root-shell three-liner if sudo or the script cannot run
  - Tar extract alone is the stock stack
- Nits
  - `sudo -n -v` is not an aj test
  - Man page allows multiple profile names and `--force`
  - `active_bare` calls revert; PASTE 2 confirms the timer stopped
  - `TMOUT=900` ends idle new login shells at 15 minutes
  - Aging is aj plus `useradd -D` only
